title: Driverless Taxi Service Planned for Tokyo in 2027
paragraphs: Taxis with no drivers could soon be driving on the streets of Tokyo. Waymo, an American self-driving car company owned by Google's parent company Alphabet, plans to start a driverless taxi service in Tokyo in 2027.

On September 15, 2026, Waymo announced the plan together with two Japanese partners: Nihon Kotsu, a Tokyo taxi company, and GO, a popular taxi app. It would be Japan's first commercial driverless taxi service.

Each company has a different role. Waymo will provide the self-driving technology, the cars and the software. Nihon Kotsu will look after the cars and will take legal responsibility for any accidents. GO will run the app that passengers use to call a taxi. Passengers will be able to book rides through the GO app or the Waymo app, and the fares will be based on Japan's normal taxi prices.

The service will start with a small number of cars and grow to about 100 vehicles. The cars that will be used are Jaguar I-Pace electric vehicles. The service is expected to operate in central parts of Tokyo, such as the Shinjuku, Shibuya, Minato and Chiyoda wards.
Waymo has been testing its cars in Tokyo since April 2025. During the tests, trained drivers from Nihon Kotsu sit in the driver's seat in case they are needed.
However, the 2027 plan still depends on approval from the national and local governments, as well as on further safety checks.
Other companies are also working on driverless taxis in Tokyo. For example, the British company Wayve is working with Nissan, Uber and another taxi company on a test.
